latest.name: Voicewoven 1.4.1
latest.notes:
# Voicewoven 1.4.1

This is the update after 1.4.0, and it is a patch version: three people tested the published 1.4.0 (screen recording for everyone) in different ways, and this version fixes what they found. It also adds two small conveniences, a keyboard shortcut for the search of your meetings and **Keep video** next to the video. For Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 14 or later, signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple.

Voicewoven records microphone and system audio, transcribes meetings locally, separates voices, and organizes meetings with Tags and Tasks.

## What is new

- **Search your meetings from anywhere.** ⌘⇧F puts the cursor in the search of **Meetings** from any screen of the main window (it is listed in **Help > Keyboard shortcuts** as **Search meetings**). ⌘F still finds in the open transcript; when no single transcript can take it (several meetings are chosen, the open meeting has no transcript, or none is open), it now goes to the same search instead of doing nothing, and keeps your choice. Settings has its own search under ⌘F, and a dialog keeps its keys.
- **Keep video, next to the video.** The **Screenshots** tab of a meeting now starts with **Keep video** and the day the video moves to the Trash, one click from the video instead of at the end of **Details**. **Settings > Storage** names the meetings whose video moves to the Trash tomorrow (five, then "and N more"), and each name opens its meeting.
- **Smaller changes.** The right-click menu of a meeting, and the menu of several chosen meetings, show only the **Pin** or **Unpin** that applies. **Mark moment** pressed again within two seconds of a mark says that the mark was already made, on the card and in the floating window, and a screen reader announces it. **Meeting > Record the screen…** works while **Settings** is open. The window subtitle says "Microphone, system audio and screen" when the screen is recorded, and the card names a display once.

## Fixes

- **Screenshots.**
  - **Delete** on many screenshots is one request now, so one **Undo** brings all of them back. Before, the delete of 122 screenshots took more than 25 seconds, and **Undo** (10 seconds from each one) restored only the last ones while the rest were removed for good.
  - A task made from a screenshot shows in its meeting's **Tasks** tab, with the picture and the time, and is counted there.
  - **Copy as bug report** and **Export…** use the title you edited and the caption of an edited screenshot, with its line breaks; a caption line that begins with text a Markdown reader would turn into formatting is shown as written.
  - Default voice names ("Voice 2") are shown in the interface language on a screenshot, as in the transcript.
  - Going to a time from the tabs below the transcript brings the video into view in a narrow window.
  - A video whose file is gone from the disk no longer offers **Enlarge video**, **Hide video**, **Add screenshot here** or **Keep video**: the player, the **Screenshots** tab and **Details** say it once, and a delete asks first. A video that never produced a frame says so.
  - A short meeting no longer shows one suggestion behind a "Show 2 more" button: the button adds as many suggestions as it says, as cards.
- **The question at Record.**
  - **Enter** never records a row that the search hides. When the search leaves one row, that row is what Enter records; with several, nothing is chosen until one is picked.
  - A screen, app or window that **Refresh** no longer finds is dropped, with a line that says why, and **Record** is not offered for it.
  - The notes about the screen (how long the video is kept, telling the other people) come into view with your choice, but never while the search box has the focus.
  - When a call begins recording while the question is open, the focus never returns to a **Record** button that has become **Stop**.
- **During a recording.**
  - The last choice follows what was actually recorded: a target chosen during a recording is the next preselected one, and a change the screen helper refuses, or a late start that fails, gives the earlier choice back.
  - A failed screen says the audio goes on; after a lost permission, the card says that allowing it again applies to your next recording. A start that times out says the screen "did not start in time", and a list of windows that takes too long says the list could not be made. The focus lands on the screen card after a late start.
  - **Copy recording notice** says "audio only" again once the screen is no longer recorded.
  - The floating window's screen line keeps its state readable whatever the length of the window title (only the name is cut with "…"), and every state reads in full in every language, with a short line where the whole sentence does not fit (VoiceOver still reads the whole sentence).
- **Names.**
  - Renaming a voice to the name of another one, from the transcript, asks "Merge … into …?" before it joins them. (Renaming in **Details > Participants** still groups voices that have the same name, as before.)
  - A summary template can no longer take the name of another one, built-in or your own, in any interface language; a template that keeps its own name can still be edited.
- **Texts and layout.**
  - The first-use sheet of the screen opens at its top at a large zoom, so its title and first line are in view.
  - The bar of the video player wraps instead of scrolling the page sideways at a large zoom, and the row with **Hide video** stays inside its pane at 150% zoom in German, French and Dutch.
  - The other texts and buttons that were cut off in some languages, in small windows and at large zooms fit now.

## Please read

- **You are responsible for telling the other people that the screen is recorded, and for asking their consent where the law requires it.** This did not change since 1.4.0; the notes of that version say what each choice includes.
- **The screen part was checked on synthetic screens only.** The screen helper, the engine and the interface were tested against a recorded script of frames instead of a real screen. The owner's physical checks on a real Mac are still to come, on the published app (`docs/screen-moments-gate0.md` and the acceptance checks A1 to A16 of issue #2, listed in `docs/request-queue.md`, with the few this version adds). Please report problems with **Help > Report a Problem…**.
- **Update.** If you have 1.4.0, 1.3.3, 1.3.2, 1.3.1, 1.3.0, 1.2.0 or 1.1.0, this version arrives through **Update and restart**. Check afterwards that the microphone and system audio permissions still work.
- **Each version works for three months.** This build works fully for three months from its build date. In the last 14 days Voicewoven shows a notice; after that it turns read-only with an **Update Voicewoven** button, and your meetings, transcripts, summaries, playback, search, copy, export, backup and restore keep working.
- German, French, Japanese, Dutch and Italian interface texts were translated automatically and reviewed. No native speaker has reviewed them yet. Please report wording problems.
- Speech and AI models download separately and need additional disk space. Generated transcripts, speaker labels, summaries and answers need review.

## Validation

The automated tests, the native helper tests (the screen helper's contract against synthetic screens included), the Rust tests (both editions) and the production build pass on the exact source of this version, which is signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple. The fixes come from a test round of the published 1.4.0 by three independent testers (during a recording, after it, and the whole app), who drove the interface in two test browsers (the engines of Chrome and Safari) with stand-ins for the capture and screen programs. Independent reviews read the changes, a second round of testing used the fixed build, and their findings were fixed. Nothing in this version was recorded from a real screen: the owner's physical checks are still owed on the published app.

releases.name: Voicewoven 1.4.0
releases.notes:
# Voicewoven 1.4.0

This is the update after 1.3.3, and it is a minor version because it adds a feature that people have waited for: Voicewoven can now record the screen beside the meeting audio and keep screenshots of the moments people point at, each with what was said. It is there for everyone, with no switch to turn on: every time you start a recording yourself, Voicewoven asks what to record, and **Audio only** is the first answer. For Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 14 or later, signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple.

Voicewoven records microphone and system audio, transcribes meetings locally, separates voices, and organizes meetings with Tags and Tasks.

## What is new

- **Record the screen with the meeting.** **Record now**, **Record** in the toolbar, **Meeting > Record meeting**, ⌥⌘R and the menu bar item now ask **What do you want to record?**: **Audio only**, **The whole screen**, **An app** or **A window**. Your last answer is chosen again next time (**Audio only** the first time, and whenever your last window, app or screen cannot be found, with a line that says why), a line next to **Record** says what Enter will record, **Enter** starts the recording and **Esc** starts nothing. The first time you choose a screen, app or window, a sheet says what is recorded and for how long it is kept. A call that Voicewoven records by itself never asks and stays audio only; you can add the screen during the recording. The video has no sound, and it uses the system audio permission you already gave (macOS may ask you to confirm it again, about once a month or after an update).
- **What each choice includes.** **The whole screen** records everything on the display you pick, notifications and other apps included. **An app** records every window of that app on its display and nothing else, and **A window** records that one window and nothing else. Voicewoven's own windows (the main window, the floating window and its menus) are never in the video.
- **Screenshots of the moments people point at.** After the recording, a meeting has a **Screenshots** tab. Voicewoven finds the moments when someone points at something on the screen ("this button should be on the right", "¿por qué este campo está vacío?", "esse botão deveria ficar à direita"), in English, Spanish and Portuguese, and **Mark moment**, ⌥⇧⌘M from any app, marks one yourself. Each screenshot comes with who spoke, the exact sentence and the text read from the picture on your Mac. Accept, ignore or edit a suggestion, choose another frame, add a screenshot at any point of the video, make a task from a screenshot (the task remembers it), copy it as a bug report or as an image, or export a selection. The video plays in step with the transcript.
- **Change or stop the screen during a recording.** **Now**, the **Meeting** menu and the menu bar menu offer **Record the screen…** (or **Change what is recorded…**), **Pause screen**, **Mark moment** and **Stop recording the screen**; the floating window has **Mark moment**, **Pause screen** and a button that opens the choice. Turn the screen on late, go from the whole screen to an app or a window, and turn it off and on again, as often as you like in one recording; the video stays one file.
- **Keep the video as long as you want.** The video moves to the macOS Trash 7 days after its screenshots are saved, and the screenshots stay. **Settings > Recording > Screen** has **Keep screen video** (7 or 30 days after the screenshots, **Until I remove it**, **Until screenshots are saved**) and the **Mark moment shortcut**; **Keep video**, **Remove video…** and **Restore video** are in the meeting's **Details**; **Settings > Storage** counts the video and the screenshots apart. New settings apply to new recordings.
- **Nothing leaves your Mac.** Audio and screen video never leave your Mac. MCP never exposes audio, video or screenshots, and a summary, **Ask** and cloud AI never see a screenshot, its caption or the text read from it. A backup copies the whole meeting folder, so it holds the video and the screenshots too.
- **The macOS permission text** now says that the screen is recorded only when you choose it, in the eight languages: "Voicewoven records system audio from your meetings and, only when you choose it, the screen, app or window you pick."

## Please read

- **You are responsible for telling the other people that the screen is recorded, and for asking their consent where the law requires it.** What is on a screen (other people's faces, messages, documents) can be more than they expected, and the rules differ by place; this is not legal advice. **Copy recording notice** says that a screen, app or window is recorded when you have chosen one, and **Pause screen** stops the video at once while the audio goes on.
- **Screen sharing and notifications.** A whole-screen video shows everything on that display: the shared screen of a call, notifications from other apps and messages. Choose **An app** or **A window** when you do not want that. A protected window (a DRM video, for example) is not captured, and the card on **Now** says so.
- **The screen part was checked on synthetic screens only.** The screen helper, the engine and the interface were tested against a recorded script of frames instead of a real screen, and the owner's physical checks on a real Mac are still to come: the owner decided on 2026-10-27 to publish this version first and run them on the published app (`docs/screen-moments-gate0.md` and the acceptance checks A1 to A16 of issue #2, listed in `docs/request-queue.md`). How it behaves with your displays, apps, notifications, sleep and long meetings is what the first people to use it will learn; please report problems with **Help > Report a Problem…**.
- **The audio is the priority.** The screen is recorded by a separate program, and a failure of it, of its file or of a permission never stops the audio; the card on **Now** then says what happened. If your Mac is short of space, the screen pauses first.
- **Update.** If you have 1.3.3, 1.3.2, 1.3.1, 1.3.0, 1.2.0 or 1.1.0, this version arrives through **Update and restart**. Check afterwards that the microphone and system audio permissions still work. An older `screenMoments` setting in `preferences.json` is ignored.
- **Each version works for three months.** This build works fully for three months from its build date. In the last 14 days Voicewoven shows a notice; after that it turns read-only with an **Update Voicewoven** button, and your meetings, transcripts, summaries, playback, search, copy, export, backup and restore keep working.
- German, French, Japanese, Dutch and Italian interface texts were translated automatically and reviewed. No native speaker has reviewed them yet. Please report wording problems.
- Speech and AI models download separately and need additional disk space. Generated transcripts, speaker labels, summaries and answers need review.

## Validation

The automated tests, the native helper tests (the screen helper's contract against synthetic screens included), the Rust tests (both editions) and the production build pass on the exact source of this version, which is signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple. Independent reviews read the change, and testers drove the interface in two test browsers (the engines of Chrome and Safari) with stand-ins for the capture and screen programs, at the smallest window and the largest zoom, in English and German; their findings were fixed and checked again. Nothing in this version was recorded from a real screen: Gate 0 and A1 to A16 are still owed by the owner on the published app.

releases.name: Voicewoven 1.3.3
releases.notes:
# Voicewoven 1.3.3

This is the update after 1.3.2, and it is a patch version with two fixes and nothing new: Voicewoven now runs only once at a time, and the smallest window at a large zoom keeps the list and the open meeting in view. For Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 14 or later, signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple.

Voicewoven records microphone and system audio, transcribes meetings locally, separates voices, and organizes meetings with Tags and Tasks.

## Fixes

- **Only one Voicewoven runs at a time.** Opening Voicewoven a second time, from another copy of the app too, now brings the one that is open forward (and its window back, if you had closed it) and the second one quits, so two copies can never write to the same library. Voicewoven already tried to do this, but it gave up when its way of finding the running copy failed, and then two copies ran, each with its own engine saving to the same meetings. It now also takes a lock on its data folder before it starts anything. macOS keeps the lock, so it ends at once when the app ends, even in a crash, and **Update and restart** is not affected. The lock is the small file `instance.lock` in the data folder: it holds only a process number, is not in backups and is never moved to the Trash by **Erase all meetings and data…**.
- **A small window at a large zoom.** In the smallest window at 175% and 200% zoom, the line that says a run of **Transcribe all meetings again…** was cut short is one short row, so a meeting stays in view in **Meetings**; the counts beside **Meetings** and **Tasks** in the sidebar never lose a digit (a long name ends in "…" instead); and the toolbars of **Meetings** and **Tasks** keep three rows in every language, so the open meeting keeps its room.

## Please read

- **Update.** If you have 1.3.2, 1.3.1, 1.3.0, 1.2.0 or 1.1.0, this version arrives through **Update and restart**. Check afterwards that the microphone and system audio permissions still work.
- **Each version works for three months.** This build works fully for three months from its build date. In the last 14 days Voicewoven shows a notice; after that it turns read-only with an **Update Voicewoven** button, and your meetings, transcripts, summaries, playback, search, copy, export, backup and restore keep working.
- **Not yet observed on a Mac:** opening Voicewoven a second time (from a second copy of the app too, and with its window closed) and the restart after an update were tested with real processes on a temporary folder, but not in the installed app. The small windows were measured with the real style sheet in test browsers, not in the real window. The checks on a real Mac are listed in `docs/request-queue.md`.
- **A limit that remains.** The lock belongs to the app, not yet to its engine. If the app crashes, the engine still needs a few seconds to save and end; opening Voicewoven again in those seconds can start a second engine.
- German, French, Japanese, Dutch and Italian interface texts were translated automatically and reviewed. No native speaker has reviewed them yet. Please report wording problems.
- Speech and AI models download separately and need additional disk space. Generated transcripts, speaker labels, summaries and answers need review.

## Validation

The automated tests, the native helper tests, the Rust tests (both editions) and the production build pass on the exact source of this version, which is signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple. The lock was tested with real processes on temporary folders: a second request for it fails while the first is held and succeeds after the first process ends, a process the app starts does not keep it, and a folder that cannot hold it lets the app start with a line in the log. An independent review read the change and its findings were fixed. The small-window fixes were measured in test browsers with the app's own styles. Opening a second copy of the app, with its window closed, and the restart after an update have not been looked at on a Mac yet, which is why the physical checks remain.

releases.name: Voicewoven 1.3.2
releases.notes:
# Voicewoven 1.3.2

This is the update after 1.3.1, and it is a patch version with one fix and nothing new: the small window that stays above your other apps while you record showed only the top part of its buttons, and now shows them whole. For Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 14 or later, signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple.

Voicewoven records microphone and system audio, transcribes meetings locally, separates voices, and organizes meetings with Tags and Tasks.

## Fixes

- **The buttons of the floating window are no longer cut off at the bottom.** Since 1.3.0, the small window that opens when a recording starts (300 × 88 points, with the time, the two sound levels and the buttons **Stop and save**, **Discard** and the one that brings the main window forward) showed only the upper part of its buttons: the two sound levels, one above the other, needed 50 points of height where the window leaves 32, so the row of buttons was pushed down past the edge of the window. The levels are now 30 points high (their symbols are 12 points instead of 16, and an empty element no longer takes a row of its own), so the buttons are whole. The same cut-off happened when the window showed an error message in the place of the levels (a long message made the top row taller and pushed the buttons down): a message now takes at most two lines there, and the whole text is still read to VoiceOver. The window has the same size and the same controls, in the eight languages and in the light and dark appearances. It is on by default, so this reached everyone who records with 1.3.0 or 1.3.1; **Settings > Recording > Show a floating window while recording** turns it off.

## Please read

- **Update.** If you have 1.3.1, 1.3.0, 1.2.0 or 1.1.0, this version arrives through **Update and restart**. Check afterwards that the microphone and system audio permissions still work.
- **Each version works for three months.** This build works fully for three months from its build date. In the last 14 days Voicewoven shows a notice; after that it turns read-only with an **Update Voicewoven** button, and your meetings, transcripts, summaries, playback, search, copy, export, backup and restore keep working.
- **Not yet observed on a Mac:** the layout was measured with the real style sheet in two test browsers, one of them the engine behind the Mac's web view, before and after the change, in the eight languages and both appearances, but not in the real window. One check on a real Mac, listed in `docs/request-queue.md`, is still owed: the three buttons fully visible in the real floating window.
- German, French, Japanese, Dutch and Italian interface texts were translated automatically and reviewed. No native speaker has reviewed them yet. Please report wording problems.
- Speech and AI models download separately and need additional disk space. Generated transcripts, speaker labels, summaries and answers need review.

## Validation

The automated tests, the native helper tests, the Rust tests (both editions) and the production build pass on the exact source of this version, which is signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple. The cut-off buttons were measured in a test browser with the app's own styles, in the eight languages and both appearances, before and after the fix: the buttons ended about 8 points below the window's edge and now end 10 points inside it; a test now checks that the meters and the buttons add up to the window's height, also with a long error message. An independent review read the change. The real floating window on a Mac has not been looked at yet, which is why the physical check above remains.

releases.name: Voicewoven 1.3.1
releases.notes:
# Voicewoven 1.3.1

This is the update after 1.3.0, and it is a patch version: it fixes the small gaps that the test rounds of 1.3.0 had left, and it adds two small improvements, with no new feature. When **Transcribe all meetings again…** is cut short, Meetings, Now and Settings now say so and let you carry on; the same question is in the Meeting menu; subtitle files no longer show typed text that looks like formatting as formatting in some players; and a few small layout problems are gone. For Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 14 or later, signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple.

Voicewoven records microphone and system audio, transcribes meetings locally, separates voices, and organizes meetings with Tags and Tasks.

## What is new

- **Carry on when Transcribe all meetings again is cut short.** If Voicewoven quits or closes in the middle of **Transcribe all meetings again…**, each meeting it did not finish already said "Transcription was interrupted" on its own page and kept its transcript, but nothing said that the whole run had stopped. Now, the next time Voicewoven starts, the list of **Meetings** (where the app opens), **Now** and **Settings > Recording** show a line that says the run stopped and how many of its meetings are not done yet ("Meetings not done yet: 3 of 5."), with a **Close** that removes it. On **Meetings** and **Now** the line has **Transcribe all meetings again…**, which opens the question as it always opens: the question shows what it will redo and, with **Skip meetings already transcribed with this model** on (the default), leaves out the meetings that already have the model you choose, which can be fewer than the line's count, because the line counts the meetings the run had not redone whether or not they already had that model. In **Settings > Recording** the button of the question is right above the line. Voicewoven still does not carry on by itself. The numbers follow what you do next: a meeting you redo alone (editing a turn is not a redo), or move to the Trash, drops out of the count, and the line goes when none is left. After **Cancel the rest**, or **Cancel transcription** on one meeting of the run, the meetings you canceled are not counted as not done. A single **Transcribe again** that was interrupted makes no such line. The line comes from a small file, `reprocess-run.json`, that holds the meetings of the run (their ids and the id of their transcript, never any text); it exists only while a run goes, it is removed when the run ends or when you close the line, a file written by a later version is left as it is, it is not in backups, and it goes to the Trash with **Erase all meetings and data…**.
- **Transcribe all meetings again… in the Meeting menu.** The button was about two screens down in **Settings > Recording**. **Meeting > Transcribe all meetings again…** now opens **Settings > Recording** with the question already open, in the eight languages, and the line above opens it from **Now**. The menu item has no keyboard shortcut, does nothing while another dialog is open, and clears a search typed in Settings. While a recording runs, the question opens with everything off and says why, as it does from the button; when no meeting can be transcribed again, **Settings > Recording** opens with the line that says why in view and the focus on it, wherever Settings was before (the line is under the button or, while something runs, in the model choices above it).

## Fixes

- **Subtitle files no longer show typed markup as formatting.** Many players read `<b>`, `<i>`, `<u>`, `<font …>` and `{\an8}` in the text of an SRT file as formatting, and a line with `-->` in it can be taken for a timing line. In an SRT file, text that looks like a tag or like `{\…}` now shows its brackets as ‹ and ›, and `-->` shows as `->`; a lone `<`, as in "a < b", and an `&` stay as they were said. Any text between `<` and `>` that starts with a letter or a `/` counts as a tag, because many players hide any tag-like text; an address in angle brackets, such as `Ana <ana@example.com>`, shows as ‹ana@example.com›. This applies to the text and to the speaker's name. WebVTT files already escape these characters and are unchanged.
- **The export buttons of a meeting wrap in pairs.** In a meeting's **Summary** tab the buttons come in three pairs (the two copy buttons, the two file exports and the two subtitle exports), so **Export as subtitles (WebVTT)…** no longer waits alone on a second row.
- **The question of Transcribe all meetings again… shows when it can scroll.** In a small window or at a large zoom, macOS hides the scroll bar, and the question showed only its first choices with nothing to say there was more below. A soft shadow now shows at the top or bottom edge while more is hidden past it.
- **The Close of a notice can be found by its name.** Screen readers and Voice Control name a button after its accessible label, and the **Close** of a notice (the error banner, the notice after erasing everything, the one after a recording stopped early, the one of an import and the line above) was labeled "Dismiss notice", which does not contain the word shown, so "Click Close" did not find it. The label is now "Close notice", in the eight languages.
- **A correction to the notes of 1.3.0.** They said that a meeting without a transcript has both subtitle buttons off, and a line says why. That is true for a meeting that has a summary but no transcript. A meeting with neither a summary nor a transcript shows no Copy or Export buttons at all. The README now says exactly this; the published notes of 1.3.0 are as they were.

## Please read

- **Update.** If you have 1.3.0, 1.2.0 or 1.1.0, this version arrives through **Update and restart**. Check afterwards that the microphone and system audio permissions still work.
- **Each version works for three months.** This build works fully for three months from its build date. In the last 14 days Voicewoven shows a notice; after that it turns read-only with an **Update Voicewoven** button, and your meetings, transcripts, summaries, playback, search, copy, export, backup and restore keep working.
- **The line after a cut-short run is only a note.** It tells you how many meetings are not done; it does not start anything. If you change your mind, **Close** removes it.
- **Not yet observed on a Mac:** the tests used the real engine and a browser, with stand-ins for the native helpers, so three checks on a real Mac listed in `docs/request-queue.md` are still owed: the new menu item in the real menu bar in the eight languages, SRT files with markup in QuickTime Player, VLC and IINA, and a real quit during a real run followed by the line on **Now**. The layout fixes were measured in a test browser, not in the real window.
- German, French, Japanese, Dutch and Italian interface texts were translated automatically and reviewed. No native speaker has reviewed them yet. Please report wording problems.
- Speech and AI models download separately and need additional disk space. Generated transcripts, speaker labels, summaries and answers need review.

## Validation

The automated tests, the native helper tests, the Rust tests (both editions) and the production build pass on the exact source of this version, which is signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple. A reviewer who had not written the code read the changes and found 6 problems (2 medium, 4 low), none that loses data, all fixed. Four test rounds by an independent tester followed, in a browser with the real engine and stand-ins for the native helpers, in the eight languages, several window sizes and zoom levels and both appearances; each round checked the fixes of the one before and found smaller problems, and all of them were fixed except one limit: at 175% and 200% zoom in the smallest window, the line in **Meetings** leaves little room for the list until you close it. The last round found nothing new. None of these tests can see the real menu bar, a real quit during a real run or a real video player, which is why the physical checks above remain.

releases.name: Voicewoven 1.3.0
releases.notes:
# Voicewoven 1.3.0

This is the update after 1.2.0, and it is a minor version because it adds features: five of the features that were planned for later, the quick ones. You can now export a meeting as subtitles, pin the meetings you come back to, transcribe every meeting again when a better model arrives, see what Voicewoven sent out over the network, and keep the recording controls in sight in a small floating window while a call hides the main one. For Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 14 or later, signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple.

Voicewoven records microphone and system audio, transcribes meetings locally, separates voices, and organizes meetings with Tags and Tasks.

## What is new

- **Export a meeting as subtitles.** **Export as subtitles (SRT)…** and **Export as subtitles (WebVTT)…**, beside **Export as Markdown…** and **Export as plain text…** in a meeting's Summary tab and in the right-click menu of a meeting in the list, save the transcript as a `.srt` or `.vtt` file for a video player or editor. Every cue starts with the name of who speaks, as the transcript shows it, lasts at most about seven seconds and has at most two lines of about 42 characters; a long turn is cut at the end of a sentence, or between words, and no two cues overlap. A turn you corrected is exported as corrected. Only the finished transcript is used, never the live preview. A meeting without a transcript has both buttons off, and a line says why. They keep working after the version has expired, like the other exports.
- **Pin a meeting.** A pinned meeting stays at the top of **Meetings**, in a **Pinned** group above the date groups, in its usual date order, with a small pin before its title. Pin a meeting from its row's right-click menu (**Pin**, then **Unpin**), from the **Pin** button beside the title of the open meeting, from **Pin** and **Unpin** in the pane that appears when you choose several meetings, or with **⌘⇧P**, which pins the open meeting or the chosen ones and unpins them when they are all pinned. A search and a Tag filter still list the pinned meetings first. A pinned meeting never loses its audio to the audio retention limit in **Settings > Storage**. Pins are kept in their own small file, travel in a backup and come back with the meetings a restore adds, and **Erase all meetings and data…** moves them to the Trash with the rest.
- **A floating window while you record.** While a recording runs, a small window stays above your other apps, on every Space and over a call in full screen, with the time, the microphone and system audio meters, **Stop and save**, **Discard** and a button that brings the Voicewoven window forward, so the controls are in sight when Zoom or Meet hides the main window. It opens when a recording starts and closes when it ends, from any of the places that can end it. You can drag it anywhere: it remembers where you left it on each screen and stays inside the visible area. It opens without taking the keyboard from the call and can never become the window that receives typing, so a recording that starts by itself while you type in the call's chat does not move your typing, and a Space typed there cannot stop the recording; **Discard** asks first for a recording you started yourself. Voicewoven asks macOS to keep the window out of screen sharing and screen recordings; whether a call app leaves it out depends on macOS and on how that app captures the screen, so try it once before you share your screen. **Settings > Recording > Show a floating window while recording** turns it off; it is on by default.
- **Transcribe all meetings again.** **Settings > Recording** has **Transcribe all meetings again…**, for when a better model arrives. Its question has the model and the spoken language, which starts as **Keep each meeting's language** (or choose one language for all), counts the meetings it will redo, newest first, with the length of their audio, and lists the ones it skips and why: no audio left, the sample meeting, a meeting that is recording or being processed, a meeting that cannot be opened, and, with **Skip meetings already transcribed with this model** (on by default), a meeting that already has a transcript made with the chosen model, so a run you stopped, or that a restart interrupted, resumes with the rest when you ask again. For every meeting the question says that the current transcript, with its participant names and edits, moves to **Transcript history**, where **Restore** works per meeting. The meetings are transcribed one at a time, and a meeting that fails keeps its earlier transcript and does not stop the others. **Transcribing again: 3 of 41** shows on **Now** and in **Settings > Recording** with **Cancel the rest**, which lets the meeting being transcribed finish and leaves the waiting ones as they were. When the run ends the line keeps the numbers it ended with (a meeting moved to the Trash later does not change them) until you press **Close**. The button is off, with the reason, when no meeting can be transcribed again.
- **See what left your Mac.** **Settings > Permissions > Network activity…** lists what Voicewoven sent out or opened in your browser in the last 30 days, by day and newest first: the update check and download, the transcription and AI model downloads, each request to Anthropic or OpenAI, text handed to Claude Code or Codex, and the Report a Problem page and the download and credit links. Each line has the time, the host it went to, whether it worked and its size, and a line at the top says what left this Mac today. The list holds the host only: never an address, a key, a path or any text of yours. **Clear** empties it; it goes to the Trash with **Erase all meetings and data…** and is not in backups. It lists what Voicewoven does itself: what Claude Code, Codex or another program you connect over MCP sends on its own is not in it. The Settings search finds it too.

## Please read

- **Update.** If you have 1.2.0 or 1.1.0, this version arrives through **Update and restart**. Check afterwards that the microphone and system audio permissions still work.
- **Each version works for three months.** This build works fully for three months from its build date. In the last 14 days Voicewoven shows a notice; after that it turns read-only with an **Update Voicewoven** button, and your meetings, transcripts, summaries, playback, search, copy, export, backup and restore keep working.
- **Transcribing all meetings again replaces what you changed in each transcript.** Names you gave to voices and edits you made move to **Transcript history** with the earlier transcript, for every meeting the run redoes; **Restore** brings one meeting back at a time. A run starts no automatic summaries.
- **The floating window and screen sharing.** Voicewoven asks macOS to keep the window out of a shared screen, but whether a call app leaves it out depends on macOS and on how that app captures the screen. Try it once before you share your screen in a call that matters, or turn the window off in **Settings > Recording**.
- **The network list shows what Voicewoven does itself.** What Claude Code, Codex or another program connected through MCP sends on its own is not in it.
- **Not yet observed on a Mac:** the tests used the real engine with stand-ins for the native helpers, so the checks on a real Mac listed in `docs/request-queue.md` are still owed: the floating window over a call in full screen and in a screen share, the subtitles in real players and editors, the network list after real downloads and cloud requests, a real library transcribed again with the real speech model, and pinning with VoiceOver.
- German, French, Japanese, Dutch and Italian interface texts were translated automatically and reviewed. No native speaker has reviewed them yet. Please report wording problems.
- Speech and AI models download separately and need additional disk space. Generated transcripts, speaker labels, summaries and answers need review.

## Validation

The automated tests, the native helper tests, the Rust tests (both editions) and the production build pass on the exact source of this version, which is signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple. The five features were built on one integration branch. A reviewer who had not written the code read them together and found 3 problems, none that loses data, all fixed. An independent tester then went over the build in a browser, with the real engine and stand-ins for the native helpers, in several window sizes, zoom levels, both appearances and the eight languages; it found 14 problems, none that loses data, and 11 were fixed (the other 3 are small and noted in the project's timeline). A verification round confirmed the fixes and found 3 more small ones, all fixed. None of these tests can see a real call app, a screen share or a real speech model, which is why the physical checks above remain.

releases.name: Voicewoven 1.2.0
releases.notes:
# Voicewoven 1.2.0

This is the update after 1.1.0, and it is a minor version because it adds features. It closes the gaps that the independent testers of 1.1.0 found: things a person expects to find and could not. You can now open Voicewoven when you log in, choose a microphone for Voicewoven alone, see which microphone and sound output are used, choose several meetings at once, search and filter your tasks, find a setting by a word, erase everything or restore the default settings, and read what a restore would add before you answer; the interface follows the Mac's **Increase contrast** setting, **Help** has **Report a Problem…**, and the Welcome screen says that Voicewoven checks for updates. It is for Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 14 or later. It is signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple, so macOS opens it with the usual first-open question instead of blocking it.

Voicewoven records microphone and system audio, transcribes meetings locally, separates voices, and organizes meetings with Tags and Tasks.

## What is new

- **Open Voicewoven when you log in.** **Settings > General** has a switch that opens Voicewoven when you log in to your Mac, so calls that record by themselves are recorded from the start instead of missing the first one after a restart. It is the Mac's own login item: the switch shows what **System Settings > General > Login Items** says. If macOS asks you to allow it, a line says where, with an **Open System Settings** button. While it is off and **Record calls by themselves** is on, **Settings > Recording** and the Welcome screen say "Calls are recorded only while Voicewoven is open." with an **Open at login** button.
- **Choose a microphone for Voicewoven only.** **Settings > Recording > Microphone** lists **The Mac's selected microphone** (the default, as before) and then every microphone the Mac has. A microphone you choose is recorded whatever the Mac selects, so a headset the Mac switches to for a call does not take over, and the Welcome screen's sound test listens to it too. If the chosen microphone is not connected, the select shows its name with "(not connected)" and a line says the Mac's selected microphone is used until the chosen one is back. A recording never stops for this: if the microphone is missing at the start, is unplugged during the recording, or is connected but cannot be used (another app holds it, or it gives no audio), Voicewoven carries on with the Mac's selected microphone and **Now** says so, and the notice stays while the system audio stops and comes back. The sound output still does not change what is recorded.
- **You can see which microphone and sound output Voicewoven uses, and change them in one click.** Before **Record**, **Now** shows "Microphone: … · Sound output: …" with the name of each device and how it connects (built-in, Bluetooth, USB or virtual), and **Settings > Recording** shows the same line. **Change…** opens **System Settings > Sound**, and the line is read again when you come back to the window. Unless you chose a microphone above, Voicewoven records the microphone the Mac has selected and follows a change, even during a recording. When the sound comes out of the Mac's built-in speakers, the line adds that headphones give the cleanest recording. The names stay on this Mac.
- **Choose several meetings at once.** In **Meetings**, **⌘-click** adds a row to the choice or takes it out, **⇧-click** chooses a range, **⇧↑** and **⇧↓** extend the choice, and **⌘A** chooses every row the list shows, wherever the focus is in Meetings (in the search field and in the transcript, **⌘A** still selects text). **Esc** clears the choice. The right pane then gives the count and the total time, and lets you **Add tag…**, **Remove tag…** or **Move to Trash…** for all of them. **⌘⌫** asks the same question as **Move to Trash…**, which says the meetings can be put back from the Trash in Finder. A big choice goes in batches of 200, with a line such as "Adding the Tag “Finance”… 200 of 600", so in a test a Tag on 600 meetings took about a second instead of half a minute, and the Trash no longer ends with a false "took too long" message. A recording, a meeting being processed or summarized and a folder Voicewoven could not open are never moved to the Trash, and the pane says how many were left out. If an action fails for some meetings, it names the first five, with the reason, and they stay chosen.
- **Search and filter the tasks.** A search field above the Tasks list reads the task, the person and the meeting's title (ignoring case and accents, like the Meetings search) and narrows the tasks and the suggestions as you type. **Esc** empties it and **⌘F** in Tasks goes to it. **Filter**, next to **Mine** and **All**, narrows by meeting, person or Tag, and on a task row the person, the meeting and its Tags are buttons that set that choice in one click. A line says how many tasks match, and **Clear filters** empties the search and the choices. They stay while the app is open and are not saved for the next launch.
- **Search in Settings.** A **Search settings** field at the top of Settings finds a setting from a word of its name or of the line under it, in every tab at once, ignoring case and accents and in the language of the interface. The best match comes first. Choosing a result goes to its tab, scrolls to the setting, puts the focus on its control and marks its row for a moment. **Manage models…**, **Manage templates…**, **Saved voices…** and **Learn from my corrections…** are results too. **⌘F** while Settings is open puts the cursor in the field; **Esc** empties it, and a second **Esc** closes Settings. A setting that is not there is not listed: not in the Mac App Store edition, not while the experiment that shows it is off, and not the login switch on a Mac that cannot offer it.
- **Erase all meetings and data.** **Settings > Storage > Erase all meetings and data…**, the last button of the tab, is for starting over or for handing the Mac to someone else. It asks first and counts what it will move to the Trash: your meetings (with their audio, transcripts, summaries and screen video), Tasks, Tags, your own summary templates, saved voices, corrections, audio examples, Ask conversations and your settings, name included. Nothing is deleted outright: **Put Back** in Finder brings it back until the Trash is emptied. The downloaded models, the connections to other apps (MCP) and the backups you made elsewhere stay. **Also remove saved API keys** is off unless you tick it; it deletes the Anthropic and OpenAI keys from the Keychain once everything else has moved. It is refused, with the reason, while Voicewoven records, transcribes, writes a summary, answers in Ask, imports, backs up, restores or downloads a model. While it runs, an import, a backup or a restore is refused too, and assistants connected through MCP see no meetings. If one move fails it stops and says how many items were moved; running it again finishes. Afterwards the Welcome opens with a notice, and the app is as on its first start.
- **Restore default settings.** **Settings > General > Restore default settings…** asks first, then puts the switches and the recording, transcription and summary defaults back to what a new installation has. The question says that **Record calls by themselves** and screen recording turn off and their choices go back to the defaults. Your meetings, Tasks, Tags, summary templates, saved voices, corrections, API keys, downloaded models, name, appearance and language are not changed.
- **The restore question names the meetings.** **Settings > Storage > Restore from backup…** now shows the title and date of the meetings it would add, the five newest and then **and N more**, so you can tell what is coming back before you answer.
- **Increase contrast.** When the Mac's **Increase contrast** setting (System Settings > Accessibility > Display) is on, Voicewoven darkens its text and the names of the voices, draws borders and the edge of the off switches clearly, widens the focus ring and deepens the colors, in light and in dark. The layout stays the same.
- **Help > Report a Problem….** Opens the new-issue page of the public releases repository in your browser with the version, the build identifier and the macOS version already filled in, and says you may paste **Settings > About > Copy diagnostic information** if you want to. No path, meeting text or email address is in it, and nothing is sent until you send it.
- **The Welcome screen says that Voicewoven checks for updates.** A new **Updates** part at the end of the Welcome screen says that Voicewoven checks once a day for a new version and that you can turn this off in **Settings > About**, with an **Open in Settings** button that goes to the switch. The Mac App Store edition, which has no update check, and a check that is already off do not show it.

## Fixes

- **Tasks with the keyboard.** The task list and the suggestions to review are one place in the Tab order (crossing thirteen tasks took 91 presses and now takes 15), and the focus stays on the list when you complete or reopen a task.
- **Reading in dark.** The Tag name on the selected row in **Meetings** is easier to read.

## Please read

- **Update.** If you have 1.1.0 or 1.0.0, this version arrives through **Update and restart**. The app keeps the same identity, so the microphone and system audio permissions should survive it; check that they still work afterwards.
- **Each version works for three months.** This build works fully for three months from its build date. In the last 14 days Voicewoven shows a notice. After that it turns read-only with an **Update Voicewoven** button: your meetings, transcripts, summaries, playback, search, copy, export, backup, restore and reading through MCP keep working, but recording, transcription, new summaries, Ask and model downloads stop until you update. Your meetings always stay readable.
- **Check every summary before you share it.** The local AI model can get details wrong with any template: it sometimes changes a number, invents a date or gives a commitment to the wrong person. **Accept all** accepts what the model suggested, so read the tasks too.
- **Erase all meetings and data… keeps some things.** The downloaded models, the connections to other apps (MCP), the choice of AI connection and the backups you made stay. On a Mac you hand to someone else, an assistant connected through MCP stays connected, with no meetings to read, until you revoke it in **Settings > Integrations**.
- **Calls that record by themselves still need the app to be open.** The new login switch is how to have it open after a restart; the responsibility of telling the other people that you are recording is still yours.
- **Not yet observed on a Mac:** the tests used the real engine with stand-ins for the native helpers, so the checks on a real Mac listed in `docs/request-queue.md` are still owed. They include the in-place update from 1.1.0 and 1.0.0; the login switch in `/Applications` after a restart, and the line macOS shows when it waits for your approval; real microphones for the microphone line and **Change…** (the built-in one, AirPods, a USB microphone, a virtual one, the headphone jack) and for the choice of a microphone for Voicewoven alone, including unplugging the chosen one during a recording and one that another app holds; **Erase all meetings and data…** with Finder's **Put Back**, on a copy of a library; **Help > Report a Problem…** opening the browser from the real menu; the look of **Increase contrast** in the real window; whether **⌘A**, **⌘⌫** and **⌘F** reach the page before the native **Edit** menu does; choosing meetings with a real trackpad and a large library; and the search in Settings with VoiceOver. The checks of 1.1.0 that were still owed (calls recorded by themselves in real Zoom, Teams, FaceTime, Slack, Webex, Discord and WhatsApp calls, the owner's checks of echo removal, saved voices with real people, a library of 3,000 meetings) remain owed. macOS 14 has not been exercised.
- German, French, Japanese, Dutch and Italian interface texts were translated automatically and reviewed. No native speaker has reviewed them yet. Please report wording problems.
- Speech and AI models download separately and need additional disk space. Generated transcripts, speaker labels, summaries and answers need review.

## Validation

The automated tests, the native helper tests, the Rust tests (both editions) and the production build pass on the exact source of this version, which is signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple. The features were built on one integration branch. A reviewer who had not written the code read the first 36 commits and found 4 problems, none that loses data, all fixed. An independent tester then went over the build in a browser, with the real engine and stand-ins for the native helpers, in several window sizes and languages, with Increase contrast on and with a library of 600 meetings; it found 12 problems, all fixed, and a verification round on those fixes found a few more small ones, all fixed too. The choice of a microphone for Voicewoven alone was built after those rounds, with its own tests. None of these tests can touch a real microphone, a login item or the Trash of a real Mac, which is why the physical checks above remain.

releases.name: Voicewoven 1.1.0
releases.notes:
# Voicewoven 1.1.0

The first update after 1.0.0. Besides a polish round, it adds features: calls that record by themselves, importing a recording, recognizing saved voices across meetings, find and replace in a transcript, a sample meeting and summary templates of your own. Independent testers went through every main flow, counted the clicks to reach each screen and wrote down what was unclear, slow or missing; many changes below come from that. For Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 14 or later, signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple.

## What is new

- **Calls can record by themselves.** Off until you turn it on, in the Welcome screen or at the end of **Settings > Recording** (macOS 14.2 or later). When Zoom, Microsoft Teams, FaceTime, Slack, Webex, Discord or WhatsApp has used the microphone for 10 seconds, Voicewoven starts recording and tells you with a notification; a minute after the app stops using the microphone, the recording is saved and transcribed. Web browsers only ask **Record this call?**. **Discard** moves a wrong recording to the Trash. No new permission, no window titles, and nothing leaves the Mac. You are responsible for telling the other people that you are recording.
- **Import a recording.** **Meeting > Import a recording…** (⌘O), the button in **Meetings**, or a file dropped on the window turns an m4a, mp3, wav, aiff, caf, mp4 or mov file into a meeting, transcribed like any other. The file is never moved or changed.
- **Recognize people across meetings (optional).** **Settings > Permissions > Saved voices…** asks for consent first. **Remember voice** on a participant who agreed saves a voiceprint; later meetings name returning voices by themselves, marked **Named by voice** (a small icon beside the name), with **Not Ana** to put the old name back. Voiceprints stay on this Mac and are never in backups, exports, assistants, Ask or cloud AI.
- **Replace a misheard word everywhere.** In a meeting's find bar (⌘F), **Replace all…** shows every sentence that would change before anything changes, and one **Undo** puts everything back.
- **No more doubled voices through the speakers.** When the call plays through the Mac's speakers, Voicewoven removes the call's copy from the microphone after you stop, on a copy in memory; the original recording is never changed. Headphones still give the cleanest microphone.
- **Templates of your own.** **Manage templates…**, in **Settings > Summaries and AI** and beside the template choice in a meeting, creates, duplicates, edits and deletes summary templates.
- **The first summary takes one button.** **Generate summary and tasks** downloads the AI model the first time and then writes the summary by itself. Suggested tasks are quicker to review: **Accept all**, and **Edit** right after **Accept**.
- **A sample meeting** for a new library, with a summary and decisions and no audio, to look around in. Its note has **Remove meeting…**.
- **Restore from backup inside the app.** **Settings > Storage > Restore from backup…** adds back the meetings, Tasks, Tags and summary templates that a backup has and this Mac is missing. It never replaces or deletes anything.
- **Settings is easier to move around.** It opens on the tab you used last, a new **Summaries and AI** tab holds the summary choices, and **Recording** is shorter. **Connect Claude Code** and **Connect Codex**, in **Settings > Integrations**, do the whole MCP setup in one click.
- **Small things that save clicks.** Discard a recording you started by mistake, and rename a meeting while it records. A search result opens the meeting at the words it found in the transcript. **Show in Finder** and the exports are in a meeting's right-click menu, Ask answers have **Copy answer**, and **Help > What's New in Voicewoven** lists every version.
- **Search reads more**: summaries, decisions, voice names and Tags, with the words around each match. **Ask** has its own place in the sidebar, with an **Experimental** badge.
- **A large library stays fast.** With 600 meetings, Record and Stop answer in about 60 and 110 milliseconds instead of 1.3 and 6.5 seconds, and a chosen meeting is drawn in about 50 milliseconds.
- **Large zoom, small windows and contrast.** At 150% or 200% zoom the page no longer scrolls sideways; text and controls reach the WCAG AA contrast levels.
- **Plainer messages** for a full disk, a damaged file (its data is kept), a stopped engine, the local AI and permission checks. Dates, units and quotation marks follow the interface language.
- **Each meeting remembers its microphone and sound output**, shown in **Details**.

## Please read

- **Update.** From 1.0.0, or 0.1.29-preview.1 or later, this version arrives through **Update and restart**. Check afterwards that the microphone and system audio permissions still work.
- **Each version works for three months.** From this version on, every build works fully for three months from its build date. A notice appears in the last 14 days; after that Voicewoven turns read-only (meetings, transcripts, summaries, playback, search, export and backup keep working) until you update. Versions before 1.1.0 are no longer offered for download.
- **Check every summary before you share it**, and the tasks too: the local AI model can get details wrong.
- **Names given by voice need checking.** Recognizing people was tested on synthetic voices only. Look for **Named by voice** and choose **Not** with the name when it is wrong. Save a person's voice only if they agree; a voiceprint is biometric data.
- **Recording calls by themselves is your responsibility.** Some places require everyone's consent before a call is recorded; this is not legal advice. **Copy recording notice** puts a polite notice on the clipboard.
- **Assistants connected through MCP** that may read summaries now also receive decisions and accepted tasks. Turn the content choice down or revoke the connection in **Settings > Integrations** if you do not want that.
- German, French, Japanese, Dutch and Italian texts were translated automatically and reviewed; no native speaker has reviewed them yet. Please report wording problems.
- Not yet observed on a real Mac: real calls recording by themselves, saved voices with real people, VoiceOver, the native menus and notifications in each language, and a library of 3,000 meetings.

## Validation

The automated tests, the native helper tests, the Rust tests and the production build pass on the exact source of this version, which was signed with Developer ID and notarized. Each group of changes had an independent review, and several rounds of browser-based click-throughs of the whole app, in several window sizes, both themes and the eight languages, were run on the finished branch with stand-ins for the native helpers and the AI model.
